newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power dips on cheap TVA offers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power dips on cheap TVA offers.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. dipped Friday, pressured lower by offers of cheap weekend power by Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), market sources said.
"The market was driven by those guys (TVA)...It's just really soft," said a Houston trader.

TVA, the country's largest utility, was heard offering electricity during heavy load hours on Saturday at $16.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) and Sunday $15.00, and during light load hours on Saturday and Sunday at 12.00.
Thursday's spot trading range for peak power delivered into northern portion of TVA's system was near $17.00.
Northern TVA prices on Monday for peak power was assessed at $15.00-$17.00 and for off-peak power $12.00-$13.00.

At the Georgia-Florida border, peak, non-firm electricity for the weekend was discussed in the $19.50-$20.00, compared with Thursday's $21.00-$22.00, while off-peak weekend prices was valued in the $15.50-$16.00 range.
On Monday, peak electricity prices at the Ga./Fla. border were talked at $22.00-$23.00.
Duke Power co's 846 megawatt (MW) Oconee 2 nuclear unit in Seneca, S.C., and Florida Power Corp's 825 MW Crystal River 3 in Red Level, Fla., remained off line, with no restart dates.
Florida Power & Light Co's Turkey Point 3 nuclear unit in Florida City, Fla., was expected to boost output over the weekend toward full power early next week.
The unplanned shutdowns of those units has been mitigated by cool autumn weather in the region, market sources said.
